column.text: Bitcoin is currently trapped in a brutal long squeeze where aggressive liquidations of nearly eighty-five million dollars are eroding the floor despite massive institutional buying pressure. While BlackRock and other spot ETFs absorbed over seven hundred twenty-eight million dollars today, retail positioning remains dangerously net short on major assets like Ethereum and Solana. The tape shows clear signs of deleveraging rather than organic strength as open interest declines while price action tests critical support at seventy-eight thousand two hundred dollars. If macro headlines regarding nonfarm payrolls confirm rate hike fears, we could see a flush down to test lower liquidity zones near sixty-nine thousand five hundred dollars where stop clusters await. The Fear and Greed index sits at seventy-three indicating excessive greed that often precedes sharp corrections when dollar liquidity contracts against risk assets. Traders must recognize this divergence between institutional absorption and retail leverage as the primary driver of current volatility rather than fundamental value shifts alone. Short sellers need a real mechanism such as overheated funding rates or failed breakouts to justify entering counter-trend positions into strength, never simply fading what looks extended without confirmation of exhaustion. The market is pushing against a macro headwind that demands more proof on continuation longs before committing significant capital upside. Failed rallies in this regime should be treated as better-odds shorts until the deleveraging cycle completes and organic demand stabilizes levels above key moving averages.
